revision_history: v1 (2026-05-31): initial draft after Phase 1 brief. Radar pick A5 (queue #104). Frame rotated from 'scams are rising' to 'every control point is downstream of the loss': police take the report after the money is gone, and the recruitment channel (social platforms) carries no domestic liability. RM1.47B/9,603 is the 2025 CCID full-year figure superseding the interim RM1.3B (Jan 2026).
_provenance.discipline: Process-not-victim. Cards do NOT blame victims for being defrauded; they locate the failure at the post-loss control architecture and the unpriced platform-recruitment channel. The RM1.47B investment-only figure is kept distinct from the larger all-category scam totals (RM2.7B+).

headline: Investment-scam losses jumped to RM1.47B in 2025; every control point sits after the money is gone
context: Bukit Aman's Commercial Crime Investigation Department reported that non-existent-investment scams cost Malaysians RM1.47 billion across 9,603 cases in 2025, up from RM848.6 million across 6,337 cases in 2024.

cards.big: Police logged RM1.47 billion lost to fake investments in 2025, up from RM848.6 million a year earlier.
cards.sub: CCID director Rusdi Mohd Isa gave the figure on 18 April 2026: 9,603 cases, against 6,337 in 2024.

cards.big: The second hit lands after the 'profit': victims see fake gains, then pay 'fees' to withdraw money that was never there.
cards.sub: CCID's funnel: lure on Facebook or Instagram, move to WhatsApp or Telegram, show fabricated dashboard profits, then charge processing fees, taxes and other charges to release them.

cards.big: Losses rose about 73% in one year while cases rose about 52%, so the average victim lost more, not just more victims losing.
cards.sub: RM1.47B over 9,603 cases is roughly RM153,000 per case, against roughly RM134,000 in 2024 (RM848.6M over 6,337).

cards.big: The regulator that licenses real investments lists offenders by the dozen; the police count victims by the thousand.
cards.sub: The Securities Commission's enforcement records held about 111 unregulated entities and 26 cease-and-desist orders by mid-2025, against 9,603 police fraud cases over the year.

cards.big: The question is not why people keep falling for scams. It is why every defence the state runs activates only after the money has already left.
It is a fire service with no building code: superb at counting the ashes, with no power over the wiring that keeps catching.
cards.sub: The recruitment wiring is the social platform; no Malaysian law makes the host liable for the loss it carries.

cards.big: Awareness campaigns ask the victim to be smarter; the money still moves through platforms and mule accounts the law treats as bystanders.

sources: S1 Malay Mail 18 Apr 2026; S2 Bernama 18 Apr 2026; S3 The Sun 18 Apr 2026; S4 The Star 19 Apr 2026; S5 Sinar Daily 18 Apr 2026; S6 The Edge 18 Apr 2026; S7 SC Investor Alert List; S8 SC Enforcement Actions 2025; S10 Malay Mail 24 Feb 2026
confidence: High — headline figures (RM1.47B / 9,603 / RM848.6M / 6,337) appear consistently across Bernama (government newswire), Malay Mail, The Sun, The Star and Sinar Daily, all attributing CCID director Rusdi Mohd Isa, 18 Apr 2026. Medium on the SC-bandwidth comparison: different agency, different remit, framed as illustrative order-of-magnitude, not as a finding against the SC.
needs_verification: SC mid-2025 enforcement tallies (~111 unregulated entities, 26 cease-and-desist) — Stage 3 to confirm against SC enforcement pages and lock the as-of date; if the exact count cannot be pinned, soften card 4 to 'dozens of entities' without the numeral.

Per-case averages (RM153k / RM134k) are Stage 1 arithmetic from CCID totals, not figures CCID published. Labelled as 'roughly' in copy; Stage 3 to confirm the division is fair and not misleading given unknown case-size distribution.
The 73% / 52% YoY deltas are computed from CCID figures; confirm arithmetic (1.47B/848.6M = 1.732; 9603/6337 = 1.515).
source_notes: CONTRADICTION: an interim CCID statement (FMT, 4 Jan 2026) put 2025 fake-investment losses at 'over RM1.3 billion'; the 18 Apr 2026 full-year briefing gives RM1.47B. The April full-year figure is later and more authoritative and is used; the interim figure is noted, not used. SUPERSET CAUTION: all-category scam losses ran ~RM2.7B as of Nov 2025 — a larger superset that must not be conflated with the RM1.47B investment-only figure.

_self_check.every_claim_traces_to_source: Yes. RM1.47B/9,603/RM848.6M/6,337, the five-method funnel, and the 31-50 victim band all trace to CCID via S1-S6. SC tallies trace to S7-S8 and are flagged in needs_verification. Per-case averages are labelled as derived arithmetic.
_self_check.overclaim_check: Avoided. YoY deltas use 'about 73%'/'about 52%' not false precision. Card 4 does not say the SC failed; it contrasts remits. Analogy does not claim platforms are legally liable — card and view state the opposite (no law attaches liability).
_self_check.underclaim_check: Avoided. Police figures are stated as the authoritative count, not 'some have alleged.'
_self_check.misleading_framing_check: Denominators kept explicit (cases vs losses; investment-only vs all-category superset noted in source_notes). The SC-vs-police comparison is framed as remit difference, not a like-for-like scoreboard.
_self_check.unverified_detail_check: No individual victims named. No causal claim that platforms caused the loss; only that they carry the recruitment channel without liability.
_self_check.3R_special_caution: Not 3R-adjacent. No race, religion or royalty content.
_self_check.process_not_people_check: Pass. No victim-blaming; failure located at control architecture and unpriced platform channel.
_self_check.anger_anxiety_check: Hook emotion is anger-at-process (defences fire only after the loss), not sadness for victims.
_self_check.em_dash_check: No U+2014 em-dashes in any reader-facing field. Colons and commas used.
_self_check.auxiliary_verb_density_check: Verb-driven: jumped, logged, lured, charge, rose, lost, moves. No field stacks three+ is/are/was.

pa_score_rationale: Headline figures are multiply-sourced to a government newswire plus four independents citing the same named CCID director and date. Primary regulator data (SC) used for the governance contrast. Points held back: SC tallies are secondary-aggregated (flagged for Stage 3), and per-case averages are Stage 1 arithmetic rather than published figures, so not a clean 90+.
